rows.selection_reason: With no completed experiments, the most critical uncertainty is establishing a reliable performance floor for the RNA modality, which is the primary signal in cellular profiling. config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is the simplest, most standard configuration: PCA with 2000 dimensions is a well-understood linear encoder, and singleprofile removes aggregation as a confound. This experiment tests whether the basic RNA pipeline yields meaningful predictive signal. It is the best first use of budget because it provides a reference point against which every subsequent design decision—alternative RNA encoders (scvi, scgpt), profile aggregation (avgpool, transformer), image modality addition, and fusion strategy—can be meaningfully compared. Without this baseline, any multimodal result would be uninterpretable (we could not tell whether multimodal fusion helps or whether the individual modalities are simply weak).

With only one completed experiment (config_001: rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000 → acc 0.485), the most critical uncertainty is whether the image modality carries useful signal for this task. This is the foundational question for a multimodal cellular profiling study: if image has no discriminative power, all multimodal configurations lose their main rationale. Config_010 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) provides a clean, controlled comparison to config_001—both use singleprofile with no aggregation—so any performance difference is attributable to the modality itself rather than to profile setting or aggregation. ResNet50 is chosen as the standard, well-calibrated image encoder baseline before exploring ViT-L. This experiment reduces the largest source of uncertainty (modality-level signal) and directly informs whether to invest subsequent budget in multimodal fusion or to focus on improving the RNA side (e.g., better encoders or multiprofile aggregation).

Evidence: RNA-only with PCA n2000 (single profile) achieves 0.485 accuracy, while image-only with ResNet50 is far weaker at 0.208, indicating RNA is the dominant signal source. With only two experiments completed, the most important unresolved question is whether moving from single to multiprofile improves the RNA baseline. This experiment (config_002) isolates that single variable—multiprofile with avgpool aggregation—while keeping the proven PCA n2000 encoder and RNA-only setting constant. It is the most informative next step because: (1) it directly extends our best-performing configuration with a minimal, interpretable change; (2) if multiprofile helps, it validates a key architectural axis and justifies further investment in multiprofile variants (transformer, different encoders); if it does not help, it tells us single profile is sufficient and redirects budget toward encoder choice or multimodal fusion; (3) avgpool is the simpler aggregation, making it a cleaner first test before the more complex transformer. This maximizes information gain per experiment under the limited budget.

Evidence: config_002 (rna_only, multiprofile, pca_n2000, avgpool) achieved 0.591 acc / 0.573 F1, a substantial ~10.5-point gain over the singleprofile baseline (config_001, 0.485). This confirms multiprofile aggregation is a high-impact design choice. However, we have no evidence yet on whether the aggregation method itself matters. Question: config_003 is a controlled single-variable change from config_002 (avgpool → transformer), isolating the effect of aggregation architecture while holding model setting, profile setting, and RNA encoder constant. Why this is the best next experiment: (1) It directly tests whether a learned transformer aggregation can outperform simple mean pooling, a question that propagates to every future multiprofile configuration (RNA-only and multimodal). (2) If transformer significantly outperforms avgpool, it redirects subsequent budget toward transformer-based multiprofile and multimodal configs; if it does not, we confirm avgpool is sufficient and can spend remaining budget exploring RNA encoders or multimodal fusion. (3) Under a tight budget, resolving this foundational aggregation question before layering in additional variables (new encoders, multimodal fusion) maximizes information per experiment.

Evidence: config_002 (RNA-only, multiprofile, PCA_n2000, avgpool) achieved the best validation accuracy (0.591) and F1 (0.573), substantially outperforming singleprofile (0.485) and transformer aggregation (0.519). Image-only is very weak (0.208). The only RNA encoder tested so far is PCA_n2000; we have no information on whether a learned or pretrained encoder could improve on this baseline. Uncertainty: The RNA encoder is a fundamental design choice that affects all downstream multimodal experiments. If scgpt (a pretrained single-cell foundation model) significantly outperforms PCA, it changes the optimal architecture for every subsequent multimodal experiment. If it does not, we confirm PCA is sufficient and can focus budget on fusion strategy. This experiment (config_008) is a clean single-variable comparison against config_002—same multiprofile setting, same avgpool aggregation, only the encoder changes from PCA_n2000 to scgpt. It is the highest-information next step because it isolates the encoder effect under the best-known configuration, directly informing whether to invest remaining budget in multimodal fusion with PCA or with a more sophisticated encoder.

Evidence: RNA-only with multiprofile + pca_n2000 + avgpool (config_002, acc 0.591) is the clear best so far, while image-only with resnet50 (config_010, acc 0.208) is very weak. No multimodal configuration has been tested yet. Question: Does combining the strong RNA signal with the weak resnet50 image signal via concatenation provide any complementary benefit over the best RNA-only baseline, or does the noisy image feature degrade performance? Why this is the best next experiment: It is the most direct multimodal extension of our best configuration (same RNA encoder, same profile/aggregation, same image encoder already characterized), giving a clean apples-to-apples comparison with config_002. The answer to this fundamental modality-combination question will determine whether all remaining budget should focus on RNA-only encoder improvements or whether the multimodal design space is worth exploring, making it the highest-information-gain experiment under a limited budget.

Evidence: config_018 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, concat) is the current best at 0.619 acc / 0.610 F1, modestly above the best RNA-only (config_002: 0.591). The image-only model is very weak (0.208), so the ~2.8-point multimodal gain is small and its source is uncertain. Uncertainty: We have only tested concat fusion in the multimodal setting; we do not yet know whether the image modality carries a signal that benefits from learned re-weighting or whether concat already captures the useful interaction. Question tested: config_019 is identical to config_018 except fusion changes from concat to weighted, isolating the effect of fusion strategy. Why best next: It is a minimal, clean A/B comparison against the current best, directly resolving whether the image contribution is meaningful enough to warrant adaptive weighting. If weighted fusion improves performance, it justifies further investment in stronger image encoders (ViT-L); if it does not, concat is sufficient and budget is better spent exploring RNA-side improvements or confirming the image ceiling. This single experiment reduces the most consequential uncertainty about the multimodal design at the lowest cost.

Evidence: The best configuration so far (config_019, acc=0.639) uses multimodal + multiprofile + pca_n2000 + resnet50 + avgpool + weighted. Key learned principles: multiprofile >> singleprofile, avgpool > transformer, weighted > concat, and multimodal > unimodal. However, the image modality has only been tested with resnet50, which scored very poorly in isolation (0.208). The most important untested variable in the current best pipeline is the image encoder quality. Question: Does upgrading to imagenet_vit_l (a substantially larger, more expressive encoder) provide complementary spatial/morphological signal that resnet50 could not capture, thereby pushing multimodal performance beyond 0.639? Why this is the best next experiment: It is a direct, single-variable extension of the best-performing config, keeping all proven-optimal settings fixed while testing the one major unknown. A positive result would validate further investment in the image branch; a null result would efficiently rule out the image encoder as a bottleneck and redirect budget toward other dimensions (e.g., RNA encoder or aggregation). This maximizes information gain per experiment under the limited budget.

Evidence: The current best is config_019 (multimodal, multi-profile, PCA-2000, ResNet50, avgpool, weighted; acc 0.639). We know avgpool > transformer, weighted > concat, multi-profile > single-profile, and multimodal > RNA-only. However, the RNA encoder choice in the multimodal setting is under-explored: PCA-2000 (linear variance capture) outperformed scGPT in RNA-only (0.591 vs 0.530), but scVI (a variational autoencoder learning a latent biological representation) has not been tested in any setting. Question: Does a learned nonlinear latent encoder (scVI) provide complementary information to the image modality that PCA's linear projection misses, potentially improving on 0.639? Rationale: config_031 changes only the RNA encoder from PCA-2000 to scVI_n200 while holding all other parameters at their empirically best values (multi-profile, ResNet50, avgpool, weighted). This is a clean single-variable test that reduces uncertainty about whether the RNA encoder's representational style matters in the multimodal context, and it avoids repeating any prior configuration. If scVI matches or beats PCA, it opens a new optimization axis; if it underperforms, we confirm PCA is optimal and can redirect budget to other levers.

The current best configuration is config_031 (scvi_n200 + resnet50 + avgpool + weighted, acc=0.6776). The image modality clearly contributes value (multimodal >> RNA-only), and the image encoder choice is a key design dimension with residual uncertainty: with pca_n2000, resnet50 (0.6390) and imagenet_vit_l (0.6352) were nearly equivalent, but their interaction with the richer scvi_n200 representation is untested. Config_037 makes a single-variable change (resnet50 → imagenet_vit_l) from the current best, directly testing whether a stronger pretrained image encoder can further complement scvi_n200's learned representation. This is the most logical exploitation step: if it improves, we gain a new best; if it does not, we confirm resnet50 is sufficient and can redirect budget toward other dimensions (e.g., aggregation or RNA encoder alternatives). Under the limited budget, this single-variable test from the top performer maximizes expected information gain about the image-encoder choice in the most promising operating regime.
